description: Intent i015 (SNAPSHOT=s04, BRANCH=uapi-double-fetch) concluded with an evidence-backed negative result. A whole-tree static scan of snapshots/s04 (function-level heuristic matching multiple get_user/copy_from_user/strncpy_from_user calls sharing the same user pointer, ~126KB of raw candidate functions persisted under the agent-state tool-results path) surfaced the main double-fetch-looking clusters. Ten highest-signal candidates were deeply read: (1) kernel/signal.c sys_rt_sigaction (~line 4425) — SAFE: struct sigaction copied once via copy_from_user into new_sa and only the kernel copy passed to do_sigaction; (2) fs/xattr.c setxattr_copy (~line 574) — SAFE: name copied once via strncpy_from_user into ctx->kname, consumers use the kernel copy; (3) drivers/scsi/hpsa.c CCISS_BIG_PASSTHRU (~lines 6537/6662) — UNRESOLVED: header fetched once into kernel struct, per-SG copy_from_user loop walks user data_ptr and post-completion copy_to_user re-reads user memory, but no field is provably validated on one fetch and used from a second fetch of the same address; (4) fs/aio.c io_submit (~line 1864) — UNRESOLVED: iocb fetched once, but user iocb memory is re-accessed at completion for result write-back (not a validated-then-used value); (5-10) net/ethtool/ioctl.c (lines 116, 1048), drivers/input/misc/uinput.c, net/ipv4/ip_sockglue.c, fs/userfaultfd.c, drivers/xen/privcmd.c — all SAFE: each user location fetched once into a kernel local, repeated fetches are of distinct offsets or distinct ioctl branches. No candidate in s04 showed a validate-then-re-fetch of the same user-memory location feeding kernel state, so findings list is empty. Bounded limitations: remaining unexamined scan clusters include arch/*/kernel/signal*.c sigframe multi-fetches, drivers/vhost/vhost.c, net/sctp/socket.c, net/ipv6/ip6mr.c, drivers/comedi/comedi_fops.c, sound/pci/emu10k1/emufx.c; no compiler-based double-fetch detector or runtime reproducer was run; selftests hits excluded as userspace. Final artifact written to agent-state/findings/i015.json and checkpoint updated.
